correctness.rationale: For any nontrivial finite product of equilateral q_i-letter coordinates with Hamming metric and distinguished 0, compatible one-vertex-at-a-time prefix retractions have exact minimum maximal Lipschitz constant 1 in dimension one or for the binary square, and 2 otherwise. A support-cardinality then support-lex order and last-nonzero-coordinate ancestor chain makes every prefix retraction 2-Lipschitz by checking each unit graph edge, including mixed kth/k-1th support projections. For the lower bound, the penultimate retraction deleting v must send v to u≠v, but except in the two stated families there exists a neighbor w of v with d(u,w)>=2, forcing Lip>=2. The explicit nonexpansive binary-square chain closes the exceptions. Linearizing gives real Lipschitz-free Schauder basis projections with norm<=2; claim is NOT an optimum among arbitrary linear bases.
residual_risks: Do not conflate retractional optimum with unrestricted free-space Schauder basis constants.
Finite prefix checks only corroborate the general edge argument.
